title: Attempting to continue the principal-prime phase law to the critical boundary
question: can the exact s=2 principal-prime anchor identity be conserved under the zero-support flow by transporting an Euler-product phase formula from sigma>1 to sigma=1/2?

verdict.conclusion: An exact weighted argument transform converts the Euler-product phase at every sigma>1 into the absolutely convergent moment -sum Lambda(n)n^(-(sigma+3/2)). Including the endpoint factor s-1 gives 1/(sigma+1/2) minus that moment. At sigma=1/2 its formal endpoint is exactly 1-sum Lambda(n)/n^2, the endpoint-completed prime anchor at s=2. Moving the contour from sigma>1 to the critical boundary crosses every zero with beta>1/2; their Blaschke residues sum to the nonnegative Euler-anchor defect. Proving defect-free continuation is therefore equivalent to RH, not a consequence of dominated convergence or analytic continuation of the prime series.

weightedPrimePhaseLaw.phase: S_sigma(T)=arg zeta(sigma+iT)/pi with the Euler-product branch
weightedPrimePhaseLaw.transform: I(sigma)=(6/pi) integral_0^infinity T arg zeta(sigma+iT)/(T^2+9/4)^2 dT
derivation: the imaginary part contributes -sin(T log n)
integral T sin(bT)/(T^2+a^2)^2 dT=pi b exp(-ab)/(4a)
at a=3/2 the prefactor 6/(4a) equals one

criticalBoundaryTarget.zetaPoleCorrection: the boundary endpoint phase is 5/6 rather than the formal value 1, producing the -1/6 correction
criticalBoundaryTarget.equivalence: D_2=0 iff the endpoint-completed prime phase law reaches sigma=1/2 without a zero-crossing defect iff RH

zeroCrossingAudit.mechanism: log zeta has no single holomorphic branch across a zero; shifting the vertical line from sigma>1 to sigma=1/2 acquires argument/Blaschke contributions from beta>1/2
zeroCrossingAudit.sign: strictly positive for every off-line nontrivial quartet
zeroCrossingAudit.consequence: the desired scalar conservation is exactly the assertion that no zero-crossing contribution exists

failedClosureRoutes.failure: growth in T is integrable, but branches of arg zeta are not uniform through zeros; the missing finite jump is the positive defect

failedClosureRoutes.route: analytic continuation of the prime moment
failedClosureRoutes.failure: -sum Lambda(n)n^(-(sigma+3/2)) continues as a scalar function, but identity theorem cannot continue an equality whose left side uses a logarithm crossing zeros
reflection sends beta>1/2 to beta<1/2; only the right member is crossed before the critical line, so the defects do not cancel
the support law is dissipative rather than Hamiltonian; the s=2 anchor is a strict Lyapunov quantity off the line, not a conserved observable
it would justify the zero-free continuation, but its required all-scale estimate is itself RH-equivalent

minimalRemainingStatement: prove that the weighted Euler-product phase identity has no Blaschke jump as sigma decreases from greater than one to one half
status: the conservation law is proved only in the Euler half-plane; its critical-boundary extension and RH remain open
